tag: Sprint 14 Task E, F117 (F114 cloud read)

bne-problem-definition: Section 2, p.4, Eq. (3): the paper states the BNE problem in full, credited to Gyurik et al. but adopted as the problem it solves.
betti-number-definition: Section 2, p.3: beta_k := dim H_k, then beta_k := dim ker(Delta_k) via the Hodge theorem, Eq. (2).
vietoris-rips-construction: Section 2, p.3: the passage states the edge rule D(xi,xj) <= eps and the k-clique to k-simplex rule.
algorithm-three-components: Section 3, p.4: the passage lists components (a), (b), (c) as the paper's own algorithm design.
input-is-pairwise-distances-edges: Section 1, p.2 and Section 3, p.5: the authors state the input model of their own algorithm.
data-defined-laplacian-form: Section 3, p.5: the passage writes Delta = P_Gamma B P_Gamma B P_Gamma and Delta_k = P_k Delta P_k as the paper's own operator definitions.
theorem-1-excludes-hardware-noise: Appendix C.1, p.28: the authors state hardware noise is hard to characterize and that repeated experiments and statistics are needed; Section 3, p.6 lists only approximation, trace-estimator and shot-noise errors.
cube-is-not-vietoris-rips: Appendix A.1, p.18: the authors state the 8-vertex cube is not a Vietoris-Rips complex and is a 3D hole example.
noisy-simulation-setup: Section 4, p.8-9: the passage states the choice of complexes, vectors and shots, the Chebyshev parameter choice and the 0.5 tolerance with its rounding reason.
cmb-experiment-setup: Appendix D.2, p.32-34: n=64 points in 3D, Gaussian and exponential, zero mean and unit variance, 50 sets (30 train, 20 test), GUDHI persistence diagrams, BayesTDA, AUC all stated.
earlier-version-flaw-qubitization: Appendix B.3 footnote 6, p.25: the authors state an earlier version without qubitization had key limitations pointed out by two readers; Acknowledgements p.10 thank them for a flaw in an earlier version.
conclusion-future-directions: Section 5, p.9: the authors list what remains open (deployment on sparsely connected devices, speedups under more general settings, practical domain problems).
akhtyamov-design-bound-setup: Section 4, p.3 and Section 1, p.2: states the permitted edits, no fine-tuning, digest pinning and that no model is pinned in the simulation.
akhtyamov-admission-rule: Section 5.1, Eq. (1) and Table 2: the gate is defined as a paired 95% lower bound > 0 plus a regression share on C of at most epsilon = 0.005, with the reason for non-zero epsilon.
akhtyamov-admission-is-a-write: Section 5.1, p.4: the record schema is listed and rejections use the same schema.
akhtyamov-feedback-model: Section 5.2, p.4: windows of 500, all flags reviewed, 5% of clears audited; 'deliberate and realistic' is the authors' own label for the simulated model.
akhtyamov-loops-setup: Section 5.2, p.4: local loop edit size, global loop typed library of two checks, same gate with no privileged path.
akhtyamov-shift-families: Section 6.1, p.5: rule v1 and the three v2 re-interpretations (threshold, scope, structural with 30/50/70% multi-layer chains) are defined.
akhtyamov-stream-and-seeds: Table 2 p.6 and Section 6.4: 23,000 alerts, T=70%, windows, 3,450 held-out alerts, 10 seeds, 9 cells, 90 runs.
akhtyamov-relabelling-design: Section 6.2, p.5-6: relabelling by rule v2 is a stated design commitment, with the supervised-at-rule-level and mis-encoded-rule risk stated.
akhtyamov-arm-definitions: Section 6.3, p.6: the no-gate and stale-label arms are defined as stated.
akhtyamov-metric-definitions: Section 6.4, p.6: rates, false admissions, and means with 95% t-intervals clipped to [0,100] are defined as stated.
akhtyamov-division-by-construction: Section 7.3, p.7: the authors state the division of labour is in part true by construction.
akhtyamov-tolerance-protective-side-unme: Section 7.6, p.10: the authors state no harmful change was admitted at either value so the protective side is not measured.
akhtyamov-mapping-limits: Table 7 caption p.11 and Section 8: design argument not compliance opinion; Article 10 bias monitoring has no mechanism or evidence; no examiner review.
akhtyamov-silent-decision-definition: Section 9, p.11: the silent-decision rate and the undecidable-case condition are defined as stated.
akhtyamov-recovery-layer-parametric: Section 9, p.12: the recovery layer is a parametric model (0.85 detect, 0.92 correct) and the run shows where failure concentrates, not how well an implementation repairs it.
akhtyamov-execution-noise-model: Table 2 p.6 and Section 10, p.12: 2% flip, shared draw (common random numbers); the authors state real LLM noise is not shared, which would raise the noise floor.
akhtyamov-false-admission-audit-weak: Section 10, p.12: the authors state the audit is weak by construction (interleaved halves, same deterministic rule), so zero false admissions on Hval is expected.
akhtyamov-synthetic-assumptions: Section 10, p.12: synthetic throughout; the miss-versus-false-positive visibility asymmetry is an assumption of unknown size.
akhtyamov-llm-proposer-not-tested: Section 10, p.12: the track tests the bound and gate, not proposal quality; LLM proposals outside the tested space are left to future work.
akhtyamov-baselines-not-run: Section 10, p.12: stated outright that no static prompt-optimisation baseline or direct implementation of cited methods was run.
akhtyamov-single-primitive-single-shift: Section 10, p.12: interacting primitives and concurrent shifts untested; relabelled pool only as correct as the rule; no protected attributes, no fairness claim.
akhtyamov-threat-model: Section 3, p.3: the five failure modes F1 to F5 are listed as the design basis, with F5 stated as not mitigated.
akhtyamov-auditability-not-reproducibili: Section 4, p.4: the log gives auditability; the authors state reproducibility of behaviour is not delivered on a hosted model and say why.
akhtyamov-cost-of-bound: Section 4, p.4: the authors state the cost of the bound is real and name what falls outside the loop.
akhtyamov-deterministic-labels-no-llm-ju: Section 2, p.2: stated that all numbers use deterministic labels and no LLM judge is used in the results.
akhtyamov-generative-ai-and-data-availab: Declarations, p.13: the Claude use, the statement that no generative AI is a component of the experiments, and the repository and release v0.6.0 are stated.
akhtyamov-no-supervisor-review: Section 1, p.2: 'No supervisor has reviewed the mapping' is the authors' own scope statement (repeated in Section 8).
akhtyamov-synthetic-no-llm: Section 1 p.2 and Section 10 p.12: the proposer is a seeded search, all data are synthetic, and the agent is a deterministic rule with a 2% outcome flip; the added agent detail is in Section 10.
akpinar-datasets-breast-tcga: Section II.A: 699 Wisconsin patients (458/241); TCGA 862 minus 23 excluded gives 839 (487 LGG, 352 HGG).
akpinar-preprocessing-pca-5: Section II.A.b: PCA to the first 5 dimensions for both datasets; the authors state PCA does not guarantee the most discriminative components (said of PCA in general).
akpinar-simulators-repetitions: Section III: PennyLane 0.35.1; ZFeatureMap and ZZFeatureMap with repetition 2 on lightning.qubit, others repetition 1 on default.qubit.
akpinar-setup-nine-maps-pca5: Abstract and Section V: nine feature maps and PCA value 5 'considering the limitations of the NISQ computers' are stated by the authors.
expressibility-definition-kl: Section 2.3, p.4, Eq. (1): expressibility is defined as KL divergence of the PQC fidelity distribution from the Haar one; lower means more expressible. The definition is taken from Sim et al. but the paper states and uses it as its own.
random-pqc-generation-setup: Section 3.1.1, p.5: gate sets, construction layers, 1 to 10 qubits and up to three repetitions are stated.
ground-truth-expressibility-procedure: Section 3.1.2, p.5: 5,000 runs, histogram bin size 75, transpilation to native gates, Eq. (1).
dataset-composition-and-backends: Section 3.1.2, p.5: 3,000 per 1 to 8 qubits plus 500 each for 9 and 10 gives 25,000 on the noiseless simulator; 4,000 on each of three noisy backends.
evaluation-circuit-sets: Section 3.1.3, p.6: 64 RealAmplitudes circuits (up to four qubits and four repetitions) and 19 Sim et al. reference circuits with up to three repetitions.
gnn-architecture: Section 3.2.2, p.7: three TransformerConv layers, global mean pooling, three FC layers for global features, three-layer regressor, one output, Huber loss.
node-feature-encoding: Section 3.2.1, p.6-7: length-23 vector (6 node type, 10 qubit, 7 noise) and the global feature set.
aktar-2024-training-setup: Section 4.1, p.7-8: 70/10/20 split of the n<=8 PQCs, Adam, 300 epochs, lr 1e-4, weight decay 1e-6, batch size 1,500, Huber loss.
gnn-expressibility-dataset: Abstract p.1 and Section 3.1.2 p.5: dataset composition (25,000 noiseless, 3 x 4,000 noisy) is the paper's own setup; the value states composition, not a result.
clamp-dataset-size-split: Section III, p.3-4: 5,210 rows split into 20 subsets from 5% to 100% in 5% steps.
clamp-dataset-features: Section IV.A, p.4: ClaMP_raw and ClaMP_Integrated; 68 selected features (28 raw, 26 expanded, 14 derived). Note: Section IV.B gives 108 columns; the paper does not reconcile the two counts.
clamp-column-count: Section IV.B, p.4: 108 columns including one target. Note: differs from the 68 features in Section IV.A; the paper does not reconcile them.
pca-16-components-qubit-limit: Section IV.C, p.4: simulator does not accept 108 dimensions; first 16 principal components chosen due to the qubit limit.
qnn-training-setup: Section IV.C, p.4-5: two-layer model circuit, hinge loss, labels in -1 to 1, 100 epochs, classical NN on the reduced data.
preprocessing-standardization: Section IV.B, p.4: standardization to mean zero and unit standard deviation; the 'packer type' categorical was converted.
future-work-more-experiments: Abstract p.1: the authors state many more experiments are needed to understand both models accurately, an admission that the present study is limited.
qnn-simulator-qubit-limit: Abstract/Section VI: ran on an open-source PennyLane simulator because of limited quantum computer access; current simulators have too few qubits for software supply chain attacks, as the authors state.

theory_low.fermionic-boundary-resources: Section 3, p.4: the O(n) qubits, O(n^2) gates and O(n) depth are asserted and deferred to Appendix B and earlier work (Cade and Crichigno; Akhalwaya et al. 2022); not proved here as a result.
theory_low.projection-onto-complex-mechanism: Section 3, p.4-5: an informal description of the rejection-sampling projection; the 1/zeta_k repeat count is stated without proof in the main text.
theory_low.order-projection-depth: Section 3, p.5: the O(log^2 n) depth is asserted from a circuit sketch (controlled-increment, Fourier-basis diagonalization) with no derivation.
theory_low.stochastic-chebyshev-method: Section 3, p.5-6: the method rests on cited work (Ubaru and Saad 2016; Ubaru et al. 2017; Hutchinson); 'it can be shown' that Hadamard columns work well is not shown in this passage.
theory_low.theorem-1-betti-estimate-error: Theorem 1, p.6, proof in Appendix C.1, p.26-28: the proof leans on cited Lemma 1 (Avron and Toledo) and Lemma 2 (Musco and Musco), drops the r_H dependence of n_v, assumes independent shot noise (not a condition of the theorem), and ends 'Combining the results yields the desired bound' with no explicit error budget. A sketch, not a full proof of the stated bound.
theory_low.proposition-1-chebyshev-surrogate: cross-group consistency, Rule A (coordinator, 2026-10-30): Proposition 1, App. C.1, p.27: the proof applies Lemma 2, the Chebyshev minimizing polynomial with |p(x)| <= 2 m sqrt(alpha gamma)^-1 on [0, alpha], which the paper takes from Musco and Musco (2015) by citation and does not prove. The error bound rests on that cited lemma. Gray: a Chebyshev-polynomial fact close to textbook numerical analysis.
theory_low.shot-noise-bound: Appendix C.1, p.28: holds only under an independent-noise assumption and a coefficient bound |c_j| <= 2/j asserted without proof; an informal bound.
theory_low.total-time-complexity: Section 3, p.7 and Appendix C.2, p.28-29: a gate and depth tally combined informally; no proof of the stated total complexity.
theory_low.speedup-conditions: Section 3, p.7: the authors' claim of when speedups are possible, compared with cited classical bounds (Gyurik 2020; Apers 2022); not proved, and 'can achieve' is an interpretation.
